sections.title: Recognizing the species
sections.text: This small to medium waxcap has a gray to gray-brown, sometimes tan cap that is sticky when fresh and usually darker at the center. The gills are white, waxy and well spaced, attached to the stem and sometimes slightly decurrent. The whitish stem is marked with tiny gray-brown dots or fibrils, especially over its upper half; these marks darken with age or drying. Flesh is white and odor is indistinct.

sections.title: Habitat and season
sections.text: An ectomycorrhizal species associated with conifers, including fir, spruce and hemlock depending on region. It fruits mainly in late summer and fall; timing and form can vary geographically. The spore print is white.

sections.title: Lookalikes
sections.text: Hygrophorus tephroleucus is often treated as a synonym of H. pustulatus, but some references still discuss the boundary and describe more slender forms with less conspicuous stem ornamentation. Stem dots and cap colour vary and are not sufficient alone to establish an identification.

sections.title: Status and safety
sections.text: Edibility is unknown or not assessed in the references consulted. This reference entry is not foraging or consumption advice.
